subject: Re: Renewal — segmented VPC expansion, burst clusters & term restructure
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@cardiopulse.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion: segmented VPC and extra clusters

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward our Jan renewal, our leadership wants clarity on two things: (1) adding two isolated cluster nodes for our analytics tenant in a new VPC segment, and (2) reworking the term schedule so we can front-load capacity in Q1 for an expected product launch.

Can Redwood provide a high-level proposal and any impact to pricing or lead times? Also copying Anika (VP Ops) and Procurement for visibility.

Appreciate it — Miguel

--
Miguel Torres

miguel@cardiopulse.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@cardiopulse.com>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@cardiopulse.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: segmented VPC and extra clusters

Hi Miguel — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provision two additional isolated clusters in a new segmented VPC and support a term restructure that allows capacity to be committed earlier in the contract year.

I'll outline the options below and attach a proposed capacity schedule so Procurement can see the cost delta. High level options:

- Option A (Phased): Provision one cluster in December and one in Feb; standard renewal term (12 months) with Q1 upfront invoice for the burst capacity.
- Option B (Front-loaded): Provision both clusters in Dec; extend initial commit to 15 months (term restructure) with pro-rata pricing applied to the extra 3 months and a 6% front-load credit.
- Option C (Reserved Dedicated): Add two dedicated node pools (higher SLA) — longer lead time (4–6 weeks) and a 10% uplift on base unit pricing.

I'll loop in Karthik on the deployment lead times and Monica for the billing/amendment paperwork. Attached: rdw-proposed-capacity-schedule.xlsx and network-segmentation-v2.drawio (network sketch).

Next steps: if Procurement can share the redlines they want to prioritize (term length, billing cadence, termination window), we can prepare an amendment draft for signature.

Best,
Priyom
Principal Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
--
[Attachment: rdw-proposed-capacity-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: network-segmentation-v2.drawio (diagram)]

Priyom — quick ops input:

- Lead time: for isolated clusters in a new VPC we need ~3 business days for infra prep (networking + IP allocation) and 10 business days for physical capacity scheduling if they require dedicated node pools.
- Migration impact: minimal for the analytics tenant; we recommend a rolling traffic cutover and KV-cache warmup window of 48 hours per cluster.
- Security: if CardioPulse needs HSM-backed key isolation, add 5 business days for KMS provisioning in the target region.

I'll draft a short SOW blurb to include in the amendment. Monica — please flag any billing implications for a front-loaded invoice.

- Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: CardioPulse Procurement <procurement@cardiopulse.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, anika.shah@cardiopulse.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: segmented VPC and extra clusters — draft redlines

Hi Priyom / Anika,

Attached are the procurement redlines we want to discuss: (1) a 12-month minimum term with an option to extend quarterly, (2) limit on termination liability to 60 days of committed spend, (3) require service credits if SLA lapses >2x in a rolling 90-day window.

We are open to front-loading a portion of Q1 capacity but need it to be capped at 40% of the annual committed spend. Also asking for a realistic provisioning SLA and a published lead time in the amendment.

Please propose wording for the amendment that addresses the above.

Thanks,
CardioPulse Procurement (on behalf of CardioPulse Health)
[Attachment: CardioPulse_Redlines_Dec2.pdf (procurement comments)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: CardioPulse Procurement <procurement@cardiopulse.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel@cardiopulse.com>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@cardiopulse.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: segmented VPC and extra clusters — amendment proposal

Team — thanks for the redlines. I've attached an amendment draft that: (a) sets a 12-month minimum term with an auto-extension option, (b) limits termination liability to 60 days of committed spend, (c) defines SLA credit triggers per your ask, and (d) includes a provisioning SLA of 10 business days for dedicated pools (3 days for segmented shared clusters).

Pricing summary (excerpt):
- Annual committed baseline: same as current.
- Front-load cap: up to 40% of annual committed spend billed on renewal effective date (Q1 launch volume).
- Cluster add: two segmented clusters — one available within 3 business days (shared), second within 10 business days if dedicated node pools requested.
- Credit: 6% account credit applied to front-loaded amount if CardioPulse confirms go-live within 30 days of provisioning.

Attachments: amendment-term-restructure-draft.docx (with tracked changes) and the updated capacity schedule.

If Procurement is comfortable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope and schedule a 30-minute signature call. Karthik / Monica — please confirm the provisioning SLA and the billing invoice cadence for the front-loaded amount.

Best,
Priyom
[Attachment: amendment-term-restructure-draft.docx (document)]
[Attachment: rdw-proposed-capacity-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
